text:
emma: morning — noticed a spike in preemptible evictions in us-west1 around 06:12; nodes are taking 3–5m to re-register and autoscaler keeps spinning up replacements, causing capacity thrash.
raj: same. saw 12 evictions in 10m on gpu-spot-ng. logs show kube-proxy flapping then timeout on join.
sara: what drain settings are we using? default kubectl drain timeout is 5m, but pods with long terminationGracePeriod will extend it.
emma: cluster-autoscaler configured with --pod-eviction-timeout=5m, node-problem-detector marks NotReady quickly. but there's a backoff period before new spot nodes are allowed — maybe our spot profile blacklist kicks in.
mike: can we short-circuit by allowing mixed-instance pools? i.e., prefer ephemeral preemptible but fallback to cheaper on-demand p3-like nodes for critical pods.
raj: yes — we can add a 'fallback' node group with taint dedicated=fallback:NoSchedule and create a CA expander policy. then use pod tolerations + priorityClass for critical workloads.
sara: also, reduce join latency: bump kubelet kube-reserved and cgroup config? but more effective: add a node init hook that signals ready only after required device plugins and nv_peer_memory are up.
emma: here's a hook we tested locally:

```
#!/bin/bash
# node-init-ready.sh
until systemctl is-active nvidia-docker; do sleep 2; done
until ls /var/lib/kubelet/pods | grep -q nv; do sleep 1; done
# touch file that node-prober checks
mkdir -p /var/lib/node-ready && touch /var/lib/node-ready/initialized
```

raj: +1. also set cluster-autoscaler option --scale-down-unneeded-time 10m to avoid thrash.
mike: another immediate tweak: in the managed spot group, shorten the taint eviction grace by adding a pre-drain lifecycle hook that runs 'kubectl cordon/evict' faster. we can use AWS ASG lifecycle hook with SQS message and lambda that calls the drain endpoint.
emma: any objections to enabling lifecycle hooks and adding a fallback node group for canary? will open a PR.
k8s-bot: deploy started: preemptible-node-fallback (ci/infra)
sara: just a note: ensure we don't create SLO regressions for tail-latency sensitive jobs — add cost-impact calc in PR.
raj: filing that calc now, will include expected cost delta and eviction reduction estimate.
emma: thanks all. I'll draft the PR and link tests. :shipit:
